blocks.text: The module documentation describes root containment, per-intent resolution, denylist forms, and descriptor-based race mitigation. It explicitly limits the guard to defense in depth rather than claiming it is the sandbox boundary.
blocks.title: Containment and no-follow contract

blocks.text: ToolError carries a stable code and fixed message, with specialized path, invalid-input, symlink, and protected-path subclasses. ProtectedPathError discards any supplied message to avoid leaking the protected path.
blocks.title: Stable tool errors

blocks.text: Hard patterns cover credential material and sensitive directories, while user patterns are parsed into anchored or unanchored glob segments. Prefix matching treats a matched directory as protecting its descendants.
blocks.title: Hard and user denylist matching

blocks.text: Denylist compiles a caller's patterns, resolves protected directories, and checks both root-relative names and absolute protected locations. The hard list is always active.
blocks.title: Session denylist

blocks.text: Containment uses commonpath rather than string prefixes. assert_safe_root rejects missing, non-directory, broad, protected, or state-directory roots; the public containment helpers fail closed on resolution errors.
blocks.title: Root validation

blocks.text: Resolved stores the approved root and real relative components. Raw-path validation and lexical denylist checks happen before filesystem resolution, then _finish rechecks real containment and protection.
blocks.title: Resolved paths and preparation

blocks.anchor: def resolve_for_read(root: Path, raw: object, denylist: Denylist) -> Resolved:
blocks.text: Reads resolve the whole target, writes resolve only the parent and reject a symlink final name, and deletes refuse the root while allowing removal of an in-root symlink itself after checking its target.
blocks.title: Intent-specific resolution

blocks.anchor: def _open_child_dir(parent_fd: int, name: str, create: bool) -> int:
blocks.text: Directory walking uses O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY, optionally creating missing children. open_regular uses O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, then accepts only regular files and closes descriptors on validation failure.
blocks.title: No-follow descriptor opening

gotchas: The configured root is expanded and resolved, but a tool argument beginning with ~ is not expanded by _check_raw/_prepare.
Writes refuse a symlink final component even if its target is inside the project.
The path guard is defense in depth; the sandbox remains the stated security boundary.
Protected-path errors intentionally use fixed text rather than echoing the path.
how_it_works: Compiles hard-coded and user denylist patterns
Validates roots and resolves paths through realpath containment
Separates read, write, and delete final-component behavior
Walks directories and opens files with no-follow flags
purpose: This module turns raw tool paths into checked project-relative paths and provides descriptor-based open helpers. It rejects unsafe roots, protected names, escapes, symlink races, and non-regular files while keeping tool errors stable and content-free.
side_effects: filesystem stat, realpath, mkdir, and open calls
summary: Guards model-supplied filesystem paths with denylists, containment checks, and no-follow file opening.
